card_summary: The proliferation of streaming services has led to a surge in demand for low-latency, high-quality live signal transport. As a result, I expect to see increased adoption of ST 2110 and NMOS for real-time transport, particularly in broadcast environments where signal integrity and frame accuracy are paramount. The use of SRT and RIST will also continue to grow, as these protocols offer a more robust and secure alternative to traditional IP-based transport methods. Meanwhile, the need for precise genlock and synchronization will drive the use of 12G-SDI and JPEG XS for high-bandwidth applications. In practice, this means that engineering teams will need to carefully balance latency and quality in their live signal transport architectures. The trade-off here is between using high-bandwidth protocols like ST 2110, which offer excellent quality but can introduce latency, and lower-bandwidth protocols like SRT, which prioritize latency but may compromise on quality. For engineering teams, the real challenge will be finding the right balance between these competing demands, while also ensuring the integrity and security of their live signals.
body_html:
Why Broadcasters Must Prioritize Real-Time Transport and Latency in IP Signal Transport

As the global streaming subscription revenue surpasses $150 billion, broadcasters are under increasing pressure to adapt their infrastructure to meet the demands of real-time, high-quality content delivery. The shift towards IP-based signal transport is a critical inflection point, forcing engineers to rethink their architecture and prioritize real-time transport and latency above all else.

What This Development Actually Means

The recent surge in streaming revenue has led to a corresponding increase in demand for high-quality, low-latency content delivery. This has driven the adoption of IP-based signal transport, with standards like ST 2110 and NDI becoming the norm for live production and broadcast applications.

This trend is not just a response to the growth of OTT and streaming platforms, but also a reflection of the need for greater flexibility and scalability in live signal transport. With the rise of remote production, SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) has emerged as a key protocol for secure, low-latency transport of live video over IP networks.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The shift towards IP-based signal transport has significant implications for broadcast operations, particularly in terms of latency and signal integrity. With the increasing use of 12G-SDI and JPEG XS for high-resolution video transport, engineers must ensure that their infrastructure can handle the demands of real-time, high-quality content delivery. This requires a deep understanding of protocols like AES67 and RIST, as well as the ability to integrate these technologies seamlessly into existing workflows.

Vendors like Matrox, with their ConvertIP gateway, and Riedel, with their MediorNet platform, are at the forefront of this shift, offering solutions that enable broadcasters to transport high-quality, low-latency signals over IP networks. However, the integration complexity and CapEx/OpEx trade-offs associated with these solutions must be carefully managed to ensure a smooth transition to IP-based signal transport.

Impact by Stakeholder

  • Regional and national broadcasters: Will need to budget for the upgrade of their existing infrastructure to support IP-based signal transport, including the deployment of ST 2110 and NDI-compatible equipment. This will involve significant CapEx investments, but will ultimately enable them to reduce transmission costs and simplify signal routing.
  • OTT and streaming platforms: Will need to adapt their content delivery networks (CDNs) to support the increasing demand for high-quality, low-latency content.
